entries.whatItMarks: Ethiopian Orthodox feast of the finding of the True Cross. The Post Bulletin notes the belief that smoke from a bonfire led Queen Eleni to the cross.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: In Rochester in 2021 and 2022, Orthodox Christians marked it at Cascade Lake Beach on the nearest Sunday so more could attend, with a service, a procession and a Demera. More than 100 attended on Sept. 25, 2022. A 2021 cross was misread as a possible cross burning and dismantled, Eyob Adehane told the Post Bulletin.

entries.name: Abiy Tsom (Great Lent)
entries.capsule: Orthodox fast of 55 days before Fasika, without meat, eggs or dairy.
entries.dateRule: Fifty-five days ending at Fasika; start date calculated from Eastern Orthodox Easter.

dates.source: Calculated: 55 days before Fasika. Stratis Health states the length, not these dates.
Calculated: 55 days before Fasika.
Calculated: 55 days before Fasika.

entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Stratis Health describes Orthodox Christians avoiding meat, eggs and dairy on Wednesdays, Fridays and for 55 days at Easter. Mpls.St.Paul Magazine reports observant members fast about 180 days a year, and chef Tigist Feyisa saw a market among them for her vegan restaurant.
entries.workplaceNote: Stratis Health's Culture Care Connection says fasting may affect how medications are taken.
